security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, static imports, symbolic APIs, explicit local file exports, and documentation links. The eval guidance is confirmed because it can execute untrusted Python representations. Raw parse_expr input and unrestricted pickle loading add two high-severity semantic risks.

remediation.issue: The srepr example recommends eval for reconstruction.
remediation.suggestion: State that eval is only acceptable for fully trusted local data. Prefer a non-executable structured representation for exchanged or stored expressions.

remediation.issue: The interactive example passes raw user input to parse_expr.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the example with an allowlisted mathematics parser or isolated execution. Restrict permitted names, functions, syntax, and resource use.

remediation.issue: The serialization example loads pickle data without a trust warning.
remediation.suggestion: Do not load untrusted pickle files. Use a non-executable format, or verify provenance and integrity before loading trusted local data.

content.value_statement: Exact symbolic mathematics is difficult to implement correctly across algebra, calculus, matrices, and physics. This skill provides practical SymPy guidance, examples, and workflow patterns.
actual_capabilities: Defines symbols, functions, assumptions, and exact numeric values for reliable symbolic work.
Simplifies, expands, factors, substitutes, and transforms algebraic expressions.
Covers derivatives, integrals, limits, series, and differential equations.
Solves algebraic systems and performs symbolic matrix and eigenvalue operations.
Demonstrates mechanics, quantum, units, geometry, statistics, and number theory workflows.
Generates LaTeX, numerical functions, and source code from symbolic expressions.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples; successful execution requires a compatible Python environment.
Some integrations require NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, compilers, or other optional dependencies.
Not every symbolic problem has a closed-form result, and complex expressions can be slow.
Raw expression parsing and pickle loading require additional security controls for untrusted data.

use_cases.title: Verify analytical models
use_cases.description: Derive exact formulas, simplify parameterized expressions, and check results before numerical simulation.

use_cases.title: Build mathematical software
use_cases.description: Convert symbolic formulas into tested numerical functions, generated code, or formatted documentation.

use_cases.title: Teach symbolic methods
use_cases.description: Present algebra, calculus, matrices, and physics with exact steps and reproducible SymPy workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify an expression
prompt_templates.prompt: Define x as a real symbol and simplify (x + 1)^2 - (x^2 + 2x + 1). Explain each SymPy operation.

prompt_templates.title: Solve and verify a system
prompt_templates.prompt: Using SymPy, solve x + y = 5 and x - y = 1 exactly. Verify each solution by substitution.

prompt_templates.title: Derive a series expansion
prompt_templates.prompt: Derive the Taylor series of exp(sin(x)) through order x^6. State assumptions, show symbolic steps, and verify the remainder order.

prompt_templates.title: Build a symbolic model pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SymPy workflow for a parameterized matrix model. Derive eigenvalues, discuss singular cases, and generate tested NumPy-ready numerical functions.

output_examples.input: Solve x squared minus 5x plus 6 equals zero exactly.
output_examples.output: Solutions: x = 2 and x = 3. Substitution makes the polynomial zero for both values.

output_examples.input: Evaluate the integral of x squared from zero to one.
output_examples.output: Exact result: one third. The antiderivative is x cubed divided by three.

output_examples.input: Find the eigenvalues of the matrix with rows [1, 2] and [2, 1].
output_examples.output: The eigenvalues are 3 and -1, each with multiplicity one.

best_practices: Define symbols and assumptions before constructing expressions.
Use Rational or SymPy exact constants instead of floating-point approximations.
Verify symbolic solutions by substitution and test generated numerical functions.
anti_patterns: Do not parse untrusted user text with unrestricted SymPy parsers.
Do not load pickle files from unknown or unverified sources.
Do not assume every equation has a simple closed-form solution.

faq.question: What problems does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers symbolic algebra, calculus, equations, matrices, physics, advanced mathematics, formatting, and code generation.

faq.question: Does it return exact results?
faq.answer: Yes, when SymPy supports an exact form and inputs use exact symbolic values.

faq.question: Can it produce numerical functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates converting symbolic expressions into NumPy-compatible functions with lambdify.

faq.question: Can it generate C or Fortran code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes SymPy code generation workflows, but compilation and testing remain necessary.

faq.question: Does it require external packages?
faq.answer: SymPy is required. Some examples also use NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, or compiler toolchains.

faq.question: Is user-provided expression parsing safe?
faq.answer: Not by default. Untrusted input needs strict allowlists, isolation, validation, and resource limits.
